bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen Huang reinstatement sparks 31% surge; AI overhangs remain unresolved
bullets.body: Jensen Huang was reinstated as NVDA CEO with unanimous board approval and U.S. government backing, eliminating leadership overhang and driving a ~$950B market cap addition (+31.5%). Analyst targets cluster around $200-$250 (Yorkville Ives $250 on ~14.9x FY28 EPS, Mizuho $220, Needham $200); William Blair stays sidelined pending governance/regulatory clarity. Key unresolved risks: ongoing DOJ/SEC accounting investigations, MATCH Act export controls, AI capex ROI debate, and peak-capex timing concerns for 2027; shares gave back ~8% Tuesday amid broader vol.

bullets.title: NVDA: Bears cite AI token price collapse, export controls, and capex uncertainty as post-bounce headwinds
bullets.body: 22V Research argues the NVDA-led rally is inconsistent with genuine AI capex recovery — implied real yields rose despite equity gains, AI model prices fell 21% last month, and financial conditions are approaching tariff-war era tightness. Hedgeye removes AMD long but stays constructive on NVDA post-reinstatement, while noting DOJ/SEC investigations continue and AMD remains expensive on relative basis.

bullets.title: DELL: AI server revenue likely >$19B guide; FY28 non-GAAP EPS seen at $40-45 vs. consensus $30.72
bullets.body: MS TMT desk flags DELL F3Q27 AI server revenue tracking above $19B guidance, with FY28 non-GAAP EPS estimated at $40-45 versus Street consensus of $30.72. DELL was down 7.5% in pre-market in sympathy with broader chip weakness despite the constructive forward estimates.

bullets.title: HPE: Q4 beat/raise on AI demand; margin compression and peak-growth narrative weigh on sentiment
bullets.body: HPE reported Q4 EPS $1.43 vs. $1.28 consensus (+11.8%) and guided FY27 EPS $5.05-5.35 (+9.2% above Street) on 27-35% revenue growth; AI systems backlog reached $8.8B with Networking orders +56% y/y. Sell-side mixed: KeyBanc sees sub-10x FY27 EPS as attractive, but Wells Fargo cut PT to $50, Piper Sandler to $54, while Truist holds $75; key overhang is margin compression as server ASPs normalize through 2H28.

bullets.title: ADI: Q1 FY27 guided above-seasonal at $4.4B; data center acceleration expected throughout FY27
bullets.body: Analog Devices guided Q1 FY27 revenue $4.4B ±$150M (above-seasonal), with data center revenue expected to have 'significant growth' in FY27 as both power and optical segments accelerate. Q4 results beat FactSet on revenue ($4.37B vs. $4.33B) and gross margin (74.5% vs. 73.9%); supply remains tight with packaging/assembly as main bottleneck, new capacity coming online Q1 2028.

bullets.title: CRWD: Upgraded to Buy at Zach AM on 27% ARR growth + ZS acquisition; AmerX lifts to Hold
bullets.body: Zach AM rates CRWD Buy with $240 PT, citing 27% ARR growth and the $43.9B all-stock acquisition of ZS adding network security cross-sell capability. Separately, AmerX upgraded CRWD to Hold from Underweight (analyst Casey Ryan). ZS was downgraded to Hold ($260 PT) post deal announcement at current deal price.

bullets.title: META: MS notes -13% drawdown, trading at 20x '26 EPS; JPM reiterates OW $775 PT on AI product optionality
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes META is down 13% in the recent volatility, now trading at 20x '26 EPS, down 10% vs. TTM average multiple. JPMorgan reiterates Overweight with $775 PT, noting shares are pricing AI costs but not yet meaningful product benefit; META also launched Muse AI agent in UK with Walmart Agent Gateway integration live.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Down 10% in volatility, trading 14x '26 EPS; Gemini 4 gained >50% market share
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes GOOGL is down 10% in the recent selloff, trading at 14x '26 EPS vs. TTM average down 43%. MS TMT desk highlights Gemini 4 gained >50% LLM market share with users spending more on GOOGL models than OpenAI for the first time since June; stock held down by search monetization concerns despite model enthusiasm.

bullets.title: AMZN: Decart ~$7.5B acquisition to optimize AI model cost/utilization across Trainium/NVDA infrastructure
bullets.body: Citi reports AMZN is acquiring Decart for ~$7.5B to optimize AI model performance, utilization, and cost across its Trainium and NVDA GPU infrastructure; analyst maintains Buy with $350 PT. Separately, an FAA investigation is underway after an Amazon delivery drone hit a Michigan fiber cable and damaged a garage.

bullets.title: PINS: +12% on executive change-in-control agreement amendments — M&A signal
bullets.body: PINS disclosed amendments to CEO William Ready's and CLO Wanji Walcott's change-in-control agreements (effective 11/18/26), with PSUs now vesting at greater of target or actual performance on termination without cause within 12 months of a CIC. Shares jumped $1.95 to $18.85 (+12%) on the news; PINS had also been down 15% in the recent broader internet selloff per MS data.

bullets.title: HUT: Roth upgrades to Buy, $95 PT on Beacon Point Phase II construction clearance; ERCOT approval next
bullets.body: Roth upgrades HUT to Buy with $95 PT after HUT received TCEQ Notice of Intent authorization for Beacon Point Phase II, clearing the full 1 GW campus for construction and insulating it from Governor-elect Hinojosa's proposed data center permit ban. ERCOT audit report targeted Dec 10 with PUCT consideration Dec 17; satisfactory outcome unlocks project finance and IG bond market access. HUT shares were down 10% in Canadian trading amid broader crypto weakness.

bullets.title: BE: >2.8 GW incremental opportunities since late September; stock only pricing 3 GW vs. MS 6 GW estimate
bullets.body: MS sales desk highlights Bloom Energy has identified over 2.8 GW in incremental opportunities since late September, while the stock only prices ~3 GW of 2030 shipments versus Morgan Stanley's 6 GW estimate. Post-election data center environment is seen improving the fuel cell value proposition.

bullets.title: SMCI: Long thesis on 100% DC revenue growth, Google design wins, and linear equalizer ramp
bullets.body: Mizuho/Klein desk is long SMCI on 100% core DC segment revenue growth next year with gross margins expanding from 64% toward 70%; SMCI won two new Google design wins (high-speed copper cable interconnect and linear equalizer for hyperscalers). New on-board linear equalizer revenue ramp expected FY28, using 90% lower power than DSP/external pluggables.

bullets.title: GPU spot pricing +64% since June; Blackwell payback now under 11 months
bullets.body: Jefferies reports GPU spot prices up an average 64% since end of June 2026 (B300 +74% to $11.27, B200 +57% to $9.50, H200 +57% to $6.62); Blackwell all-in cost recovery payback period has compressed to under 11 months. AI XPU model forecasts 51 GW of shipments in 2027, with ASICs rising to 39% of installed capacity by 2028.

bullets.title: CLS: Down 6.6% in Canadian trading amid broader tech selloff
bullets.body: Celestica (CLS) traded down 6.6% to C$286.38 on the TSX mid-morning, part of broader weakness across Canadian tech/AI infrastructure names. No company-specific catalyst cited.

bullets.title: NFLX: Seeking bidding war for 2030 World Cup US TV rights after largest first-round offer
bullets.body: MS TMT desk reports NFLX has submitted the largest first-round offer for 2030 World Cup US TV rights and is seeking to spark a bidding war among competitors.

bullets.title: WBD: UBS upgrades Skydance to Neutral; WBD deal seen enabling streaming leadership and $6B cost saves
bullets.body: UBS upgraded Skydance to Neutral from Sell, citing the WBD transaction as positioning the combined entity for global streaming leadership with a deep library and the largest content budget. Management has stronger conviction in hitting $6B cost savings; risk/reward viewed as more balanced at current levels though high TV exposure lingers.

bullets.title: Internet group post-earnings performance: APP +37.6%, RDDT -31.5%, EXPE -24.2%, HOOD -28.8%
bullets.body: StreetAccount post-Q3 earnings scorecard: APP outperformed XLC by 38.9pp since Nov 4; CMCSA outperformed XLC by 16.9pp. On the downside, RDDT underperformed XLC by 33.9pp since Oct 29, EXPE underperformed XLY by 19.8pp, and HOOD underperformed XLF by 28.4pp. SNDK and LITE were the worst semi/hardware performers, down 47.2% and 35.2% vs. sector respectively.

bullets.title: DKNG: Sportsbook headwind from ~75% NFL favorite win rate in Week 11; 7-9% hold estimate
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags DKNG and the sportsbook industry facing a ~7-9% hold estimate for the week ended 11/22, with roughly 75% of NFL favorites winning outright in Week 11 — a significant headwind for books as the public winning percentage ran ~75%.

bullets.title: SHOP/AFRM: UBS hosting payments/fintech investor call covering tokenization, Toast 2027 modeling, Shopify updates
bullets.body: UBS is holding an investor call today covering V & MA tokenization revenue contribution, Block's Builderlab monetization strategy, Toast 2027 modeling, Shopify updates, and Q&A on FISV, PYPL, and AFRM — no specific rating actions disclosed in the invite.
